73686-my-lady-of-cleeve.title: Cleeve
73686-my-lady-of-cleeve.creator: Percy J. Hartley
73686-my-lady-of-cleeve.description: A book by Percy J. Hartley. I held up my hand and the troopers halted. The rain, which had been falling steadily since noon, had now ceased; and a watery gleam of sunshine bursting from the sullen stormclouds overhead lighted up the crest of the hill upon which we stood, and the well-wooded Cleeve valley below us, than which there is none more beautiful in all Devonshire.

arxiv-1707-01616.title: A Continuous Analogue of Lattice Path Enumeration
arxiv-1707-01616.creator: Tanay Wakhare †, Christophe Vignat ‡, Quang-Nhat Le §, Sinai Robins ∗
arxiv-1707-01616.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Tanay Wakhare †, Christophe Vignat ‡, Quang-Nhat Le §, Sinai Robins ∗. Following the work of Cano and Díaz, we consider a continuous analog of lattice path enumeration. This allows us to define a continuous version of any discrete object that counts certain types of lattice paths. As an example of this process, we define continuous versions of binomial and multinomial coefficients, and describe some identities and partial differential equations they satisfy.

arxiv-2106-03861.title: The effects of LMC-mass environments on their dwarf satellite galaxies in the FIRE simulations 2015 The effects of LMC-mass environments on their dwarf satellite galaxies in the FIRE simulations – References
arxiv-2106-03861.creator: Ethan D. Jahn, Laura V. Sales, Andrew Wetzel, Jenna Samuel, Kareem El-Badry, Michael Boylan-Kolchin, James S. Bullock
arxiv-2106-03861.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ethan D. Jahn, Laura V. Sales, Andrew Wetzel, Jenna Samuel, Kareem El-Badry, Michael Boylan-Kolchin, James S. Bullock. Characterizing the predicted environments of dwarf galaxies like the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) is becoming increasingly important as next generation surveys push sensitivity limits into this low-mass regime at cosmological distances.

arxiv-2203-12564.title: Time and Quantum Clocks: a review of recent developments
arxiv-2203-12564.creator: M. Basil Altaie, Daniel Hodgson and Almut Beige
arxiv-2203-12564.description: Abstract In this review we present the problem of time in quantum physics, including a short history of the problem and the known objections about considering time as a quantum observable. The need to deal with time as an observable is elaborated through some unresolved problems.

arxiv-2306-02679.title: Joint Pre-training and Local Re-training: Transferable Representation Learning on Multi-source Knowledge Graphs Conference: Proceedings of the 29th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; August 6–10, 2023; Long Beach, CA, USA Proceedings of the 29th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Kn
arxiv-2306-02679.creator: Zequn Sun, Jiacheng Huang, Jinghao Lin, Xiaozhou Xu, Qijin Chen, Wei Hu
arxiv-2306-02679.description: Abstract . In this paper, we present the “joint pre-training and local re-training” framework for learning and applying multi-source knowledge graph (KG) embeddings. We are motivated by the fact that different KGs contain complementary information to improve KG embeddings and downstream tasks.

arxiv-2311-00185.title: Branch-and-Bound versus Lift-and-Project Relaxations in Combinatorial Optimization
arxiv-2311-00185.creator: Gérard Cornuéjols, Yatharth Dubey
arxiv-2311-00185.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider a theoretical framework for comparing branch-and-bound with classical lift-and-project hierarchies. We simplify our analysis of streamlining the definition of branch-and-bound. We introduce “skewed k k -trees” which give a hierarchy of relaxations that is incomparable to that of Sherali-Adams, and we show that it is much better for some instances.

arxiv-2312-05174.title: High Absorptivity Nanotextured Powders for Additive Manufacturing
arxiv-2312-05174.creator: Ottman A. Tertuliano, Philip J. DePond, Andrew C. Lee, Jiho Hong, David Doan, Luc Capaldi, Mark Brongersma, X. Wendy Gu, Manyalibo J. Matthews, Wei Cai, Adrian J. Lew
arxiv-2312-05174.description: Abstract Abstract: The widespread application of metal additive manufacturing (AM) is limited by the ability to control the complex interactions between the energy source and the feedstock material. Here we develop a generalizable process to introduce nanoscale grooves to the surface of metal powders which increases the powder absorptivity by up to 70% during laser powder bed fusion.

arxiv-2312-17061.title: Bayesian Analysis of High Dimensional Vector Error Correction Model
arxiv-2312-17061.creator: Parley Ruogu Yang and Alexander Y. Shestopaloff
arxiv-2312-17061.description: Abstract Vector Error Correction Model (VECM) is a classic method to analyse cointegration relationships amongst multivariate non-stationary time series. In this paper, we focus on high dimensional setting and seek for sample-size-efficient methodology to determine the level of cointegration. Our investigation centres at a Bayesian approach to analyse the cointegration matrix, henceforth determining the cointegration rank.

arxiv-2401-14742.title: Violation of the equivalence principle induced by oscillating rest mass and transition frequency, and its detection in atom interferometers
arxiv-2401-14742.creator: Jordan Gué, Aurélien Hees, Peter Wolf
arxiv-2401-14742.description: Abstract We present a theoretical investigation of the expected experimental signals produced by freely falling atoms with time oscillating mass and transition frequency. These oscillations could be produced in a variety of models, in particular, models of scalar dark matter (DM) non universally coupled to the standard matter (SM) such as axion-like particles (ALP) and dilatons.

arxiv-2503-22645.title: A Performance Analysis of Task Scheduling for UQ Workflows on HPC Systems
arxiv-2503-22645.creator: Chung Ming Loi, Anne Reinarz, Linus Seelinger, William Hornsby, James Buchanan, Mikkel Lykkegaard
arxiv-2503-22645.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chung Ming Loi, Anne Reinarz, Linus Seelinger, William Hornsby, James Buchanan, Mikkel Lykkegaard. Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) workloads are becoming increasingly common in science and engineering. They involve the submission of thousands or even millions of similar tasks with potentially unpredictable runtimes, where the total number is usually not known a priori. A static one-size-fits-all batch script would likely lead to suboptimal scheduling, and native schedulers installed on High-Performance Computing (HPC) systems such as SLURM often struggle to efficiently handle such workloads.

arxiv-2505-04548.title: Accelerating Audio Research with Robotic Dummy Heads
arxiv-2505-04548.description: Abstract This work introduces a robotic dummy head that fuses the acoustic realism of conventional audiological mannequins with the mobility of robots. The proposed device is capable of moving, talking, and listening as people do, and can be used to automate spatially-stationary audio experiments, thus accelerating the pace of audio research.

arxiv-2510-07716.title: Computationally-efficient Graph Modeling with Refined Graph Random Features
arxiv-2510-07716.creator: Krzysztof Choromanski, Avinava Dubey, Arijit Sehanobish, Isaac Reid
arxiv-2510-07716.description: Abstract We propose refined GRFs (GRFs++), a new class of Graph Random Features (GRFs) for efficient and accurate computations involving kernels defined on the nodes of a graph. GRFs++ resolve some of the long-standing limitations of regular GRFs, including difficulty modeling relationships between more distant nodes.

pmc-10539554.title: CSNK1G2-AS1 promotes metastasis, colony formation and serves as a biomarker in testicular germ cell tumor cells
pmc-10539554.creator: Ruixue Li, Qianyin Zhou, Guangmin Liu, Fang Zhu, Zhizhong Liu, Hao Bo, Liqing Fan
pmc-10539554.description: Background/Aim: Some long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been found to significantly participate in the progression of TGCTs. In comparison to the normal testis, the TGCT tissues showed significantly decreased CSNK1G2-AS1 expression, however, its effect on TGCTs and its mechanism are still unclear.

pmc-10589885.title: Label-free approaches for extracellular vesicle detection
pmc-10589885.creator: Loredana Leggio, Greta Paternò, Silvia Vivarelli, Aurelio Bonasera, Bruno Pignataro, Nunzio Iraci, Giuseppe Arrabito
pmc-10589885.description: SummaryExtracellular vesicles (EVs) represent pivotal mediators in cell-to-cell communication. They are lipid-membranous carriers of several biomolecules, which can be produced by almost all cells. In the current Era of precision medicine, EVs gained growing attention thanks to their potential in both biomarker discovery and nanotherapeutics applications.

pmc-10738861.title: DEFENSIVENESS AGAINST INTERGROUP BIASES ACROSS ADULTHOOD
pmc-10738861.creator: Jennifer Beatty, Patrick Hill
pmc-10738861.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Research has demonstrated the pernicious role of discrimination against marginalized groups. Less work has considered the perspective of the transgressor and how defensive they may be when told they were biased. Such work is critical for understanding which individuals may be more willing to acknowledge and integrate feedback about their personal biases, allowing them to avoid future discriminatory and biased actions.

pmc-11380643.title: Wearable electrochemical device based on butterfly-like paper-based microfluidics for pH and Na+ monitoring in sweat
pmc-11380643.creator: Luca Fiore, Vincenzo Mazzaracchio, Arianna Antinucci, Roberto Ferrara, Tommaso Sciarra, Florigio Lista, Amy Q. Shen, Fabiana Arduini
pmc-11380643.description: A wearable potentiometric device is reported based on an innovative butterfly-like paper-based microfluidic system, allowing for continuous monitoring of pH and Na+ levels in sweat during physical activity. Specifically, the use of the butterfly-like configuration avoids evaporation phenomena and memory effects, enabling precise and timely biomarker determination in sweat.

pmc-11450131.title: PET radiomics in lung cancer: advances and translational challenges
pmc-11450131.creator: Yongbai Zhang, Wenpeng Huang, Hao Jiao, Lei Kang
pmc-11450131.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Radiomics is an emerging field of medical imaging that aims at improving the accuracy of diagnosis, prognosis, treatment planning and monitoring non-invasively through the automated or semi-automated quantitative analysis of high-dimensional image features. Specifically in the field of nuclear medicine, radiomics utilizes imaging methods such as positron emission tomography (PET) and single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) to evaluate biomarkers related to metabolism, blood flow, cellular activity and some biological pathways.

pmc-12595334.title: Tricin inhibits the migration of human retinal pigment epithelium cells by suppressing the RUNX2-CYP1A1 axis and STAT3 pathway
pmc-12595334.creator: Wei-Yang Lu, I-Chia Liang, Yi-Hsien Hsieh, Kai Wang, Chia-Yi Lee, Nuo-Yi Yu, Shun-Fa Yang, Hsiang-Wen Chien
pmc-12595334.description: Proliferative vitreoretinopathy (PVR) is a retinal disorder characterized by abnormal growth and migration of retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells, leading to impaired visual acuity. Tricin is a naturally occurring flavone known to inhibit the migration of various cancer cell types.

pmc-13203702.title: Research on Silver-Based Wound Dressing: An Ontological Analysis
pmc-13203702.creator: Prabir K. Dutta, Thant Syn, Arkalgud Ramaprasad
pmc-13203702.description: Background/Objectives: Silver’s ability to kill pathogenic bacteria is being widely researched in environment, consumer, and health-related applications. One topic of voluminous research is the antimicrobial properties of silver and silver in wound dressings. This research literature has been reviewed in articles using qualitative analyses, meta-analyses, systematic reviews, bibliometric analyses, and other grounded methods.

pmc-13230128.title: Ubiquitination mediated by RING-type E3 ligases in the progression of digestive system tumors: mechanistic insights and potential therapeutic strategies
pmc-13230128.creator: Yuwei Wu, Xi Yu, Chao Guan, Mingfang Zhao
pmc-13230128.description: Ubiquitination is a core mechanism for the precise regulation of protein fate, closely related to the occurrence and development of many diseases. As the most critical enzymes in the ubiquitination process, really interesting new gene (RING)-type E3 ubiquitin ligases play an important role in regulating the malignant behaviors of tumor cells.

pmc-13314558.creator: Abdulrahman Al‐Bayati, Mohamad Watfa, Nicolas A. Soputro, Lin Wang, Salim K. Younis, Karim Daher, Samarpit Rai, Rui M. Bernardino, Christopher J. Weight, Ruben Olivares, Zeyad R. Schwen, Riccardo Autorino, Jihad Kaouk, Jane K. Nguyen
pmc-13314558.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). biopsy remains fundamental to prostate cancer (PCa) diagnosis and risk stratification, yet inadequate tissue sampling is an ongoing concern that may result in missed diagnoses, disease underestimation, or the need for repeat procedures [1, 2]. In current practice, biopsy core adequacy is determined only after routine histopathological processing, typically several days post‐procedure, leaving no opportunity for intraoperative feedback or immediate re‐sampling [3, 4].
